questions.question: A restaurant manager is introducing a new digital ordering system, and several long-time servers are worried. Which approach is most likely to reduce their resistance?

options.A: Letting only new servers use it
options.B: Involving them in training and feedback
options.C: Introducing the system without warning
options.D: Telling them to adapt or quit

questions.explanation: Involving them in training and feedback. Involving employees gives them a sense of control and helps them build skills and confidence. Threats, surprise rollouts, and excluding experienced servers would increase resistance and could hurt morale.

performanceIndicator.text: Lead change

questions.question: Requiring guests to show a key card before the elevator will go to guest-room floors is a hotel security measure designed to

options.A: speed up housekeeping.
options.C: limit access to guests.
options.D: increase room rates.

questions.explanation: Limit access to guests. Key-card elevators prevent people without rooms from reaching guest floors, which protects guests and their belongings. The measure isn't meant to change housekeeping speed, energy use, or prices.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain security considerations in the hospitality and tourism industry

questions.question: Tessa, a server, is told by her manager that she must clock out but keep working to finish cleaning. Which worker right is being violated?

options.A: The right to choose her own uniform
options.B: The right to be paid for all hours worked
options.C: The right to work only weekends
options.D: The right to receive tips only in cash

questions.explanation: The right to be paid for all hours worked. Wage laws require employers to pay nonexempt employees for all time worked, including tasks done after a shift. Choosing uniforms, receiving tips only in cash, and working only weekends are not legal rights.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the rights of workers

questions.question: Which of the following can a theme park do to manage the customer experience during peak demand:

options.A: Closing half of its rides
options.B: Removing all signs that show wait times
options.C: Reducing the number of staff on duty
options.D: Offering timed reservations for popular rides

questions.explanation: Offering timed reservations for popular rides. Timed reservations spread riders throughout the day and reduce the frustration of standing in long lines. Closing rides, hiding wait times, and cutting staff would make crowding and frustration worse.

performanceIndicator.text: Identify strategies to manage customer experience during peaks in demand

questions.question: A diner tells her server she has a severe peanut allergy. What should the server do?

options.A: Tell the kitchen and confirm safe dishes
options.B: Suggest she pick off any peanuts herself
options.C: Tell her the restaurant can't serve her
options.D: Assume the dish she chooses is safe

questions.explanation: Tell the kitchen and confirm safe dishes. Allergies can be life-threatening, so the server should alert the kitchen, check ingredients, and help the guest choose safely prepared food. Picking off peanuts doesn't remove allergens, refusing service is unnecessary, and assuming a dish is safe is risky.

performanceIndicator.text: Accommodate special needs/specific requests of customers

questions.question: A customer buys a $100 gift certificate for a spa. Why is this sale valuable to the spa beyond the $100?

options.A: Gift certificates always expire unused
options.B: The buyer pays sales tax twice
options.C: The spa never has to provide the service
options.D: The recipient may become a regular

questions.explanation: The recipient may become a regular. Gift certificates introduce new customers who may return and spend more, and recipients often spend more than the certificate's value. The spa must honor the certificate, many states limit expiration dates, and sales tax is not charged twice.

performanceIndicator.text: Sell gift certificates in hospitality and tourism

questions.question: Which of the following is an ethical issue in human resources management:

options.A: Choosing paint colors for the break room
options.C: Scheduling the annual company picnic
options.D: Ordering office supplies

questions.explanation: Protecting employees' personal information. HR handles sensitive information such as medical records, pay, and performance reviews, so protecting it is an ethical responsibility. Ordering supplies, planning picnics, and choosing paint colors don't raise ethical concerns.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the role of ethics in human resources management

questions.question: Which of the following should hotel employees do if a fire alarm sounds:

options.A: Wait to see if the alarm is real
options.B: Use the elevators to evacuate guests faster
options.C: Collect their personal belongings first
options.D: Follow the emergency plan and guide guests out

questions.explanation: Follow the emergency plan and guide guests out. Employees are trained to follow the emergency plan, which includes directing guests to stairways and assembly areas. Elevators may fail or open onto a fire floor, waiting wastes critical time, and personal belongings should be left behind.

performanceIndicator.text: Handle emergency situations in hospitality and tourism

questions.question: Before deciding where to put a new coffee kiosk, the manager of the Granite Plaza Hotel spends two mornings watching which entrances and hallways guests use most and where they stop to wait. The manager is collecting information through

options.A: a mail survey.
options.C: a focus group.
options.D: a telephone interview.

questions.explanation: Observation. Observation means watching behavior as it happens, without asking questions. Mail surveys and phone interviews ask people questions, and focus groups bring a small group together to discuss a topic.

performanceIndicator.text: Describe methods used to collect hospitality and tourism business information (e.g., observations, mail, telephone, Internet, discussion groups, interviews)

questions.question: Reports show that consumer spending on travel and dining has dropped for three months in a row. A hotel company might respond by

options.A: building several new luxury resorts.
options.C: raising all of its room rates.
options.D: offering value promotions.

questions.explanation: Offering value promotions. Falling consumer spending suggests guests are cutting back, so promotions and value packages can help maintain bookings. Raising rates, expanding luxury properties, and cutting marketing could make things worse during a slowdown.

performanceIndicator.text: Discuss the measure of consumer spending as an economic indicator

questions.question: A destination management company plans airport transfers, meeting space, and group tours for a corporate client's conference. This company offers

options.A: event and travel planning.
options.C: airline maintenance.
options.D: lodging services only.

questions.explanation: Event and travel planning. Destination management companies coordinate local services such as transportation, venues, and activities for groups visiting an area. They don't just provide lodging, manufacture food, or maintain aircraft.

performanceIndicator.text: Describe services offered by the hospitality and tourism industry

questions.question: Why are luxury resorts often among the first businesses to feel the effects of an economic downturn?

options.A: They are exempt from taxes
options.C: Luxury travel is easy to cut back on
options.D: Luxury resorts don't advertise to the public

questions.explanation: Luxury travel is easy to cut back on. When budgets tighten, consumers postpone expensive, nonessential purchases such as luxury vacations. Advertising, credit use, and taxes don't explain why luxury travel declines first.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the relationship between the economy and hospitality and tourism

questions.question: Political relationships within an organization refer to

options.A: the company's donations to political candidates.
options.C: laws passed by the government.
options.D: informal networks of influence.

questions.explanation: Informal networks of influence. Organizational politics involves how people gain influence, build alliances, and get support for ideas beyond the formal chart. It isn't about political donations, government laws, or written job descriptions.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the impact of political relationships within an organization

questions.question: Under accessibility laws, a hotel that offers a swimming pool to guests generally must

options.A: provide accessible entry to the pool.
options.B: offer the pool only on weekends.
options.C: close the pool to all guests with disabilities.
options.D: charge a fee to guests who need a lift.

questions.explanation: Provide accessible entry to the pool. U.S. accessibility laws require many public accommodations, including hotel pools, to provide accessible entry, such as a pool lift. Excluding guests, charging extra for accessibility, and limiting days would violate guests' rights.

performanceIndicator.text: Describe the rights of customers in the hospitality and tourism industry

questions.question: Each afternoon, the housekeeping supervisor at the Laurel Hotel uses a checklist to inspect 10 rooms that her staff have cleaned, looking closely at the bathrooms, bed linens, and surfaces. The supervisor is using

options.A: a recruiting strategy.
options.C: a quality control method.
options.D: a promotional campaign.

questions.explanation: A quality control method. Inspecting work against set standards is quality control, catching problems before guests find them. Price discounts, promotions, and recruiting are unrelated activities.

performanceIndicator.text: Utilize quality control methods at work

questions.question: A hotel notices that more travelers are booking trips through travel apps on their phones. Why should the hotel track this change?

options.A: It may need to improve its mobile booking options
options.B: It has no effect on the hotel's business
options.C: It should stop accepting mobile reservations
options.D: It means travelers no longer need hotels

questions.explanation: It may need to improve its mobile booking options. Tracking guest trends allows the hotel to adapt, such as making mobile booking easier. Refusing mobile bookings would lose guests, travelers still need lodging, and booking trends directly affect the hotel.

performanceIndicator.text: Track environmental changes that impact hospitality and tourism (e.g., technological changes, guest trends, economic changes, regulatory changes)

questions.question: A hotel chain uses software to discover that guests who book spa treatments are more likely to return within a year. This finding is an example of using data mining to

options.A: choose paint colors for the rooms.
options.C: clean guest rooms faster.
options.D: find links among guest behaviors.

questions.explanation: Find links among guest behaviors. Data mining reveals connections, such as the link between spa bookings and repeat visits, that can shape promotions and services. It isn't used to set wages, speed up cleaning, or select décor.

performanceIndicator.text: Describe data mining tools and techniques

questions.question: A negotiation strategy that seeks a solution that benefits both parties is called

options.A: win-win negotiation.
options.C: win-lose negotiation.
options.D: an ultimatum.

questions.explanation: Win-win negotiation. In win-win negotiation, each side looks for options that meet both parties' key needs, which builds lasting relationships. Win-lose negotiation benefits one side at the other's expense, avoidance sidesteps the issue, and an ultimatum is a take-it-or-leave-it demand.

performanceIndicator.text: Demonstrate negotiation skills

questions.question: A hotel processes $40,000 in credit card sales in a month. Its processor charges a flat rate of 3%. How much will the hotel pay in processing fees?
questions.explanation: $1,200. Processing fees equal sales times the rate: $40,000 x 0.03 = $1,200. $120 uses 0.3%, $4,000 uses 10%, and $12,000 uses 30%.

performanceIndicator.text: Calculate credit-card processing costs

questions.question: Which of the following nonverbal cues may indicate that a guest is frustrated:

options.A: Nodding in agreement
options.C: Leaning forward with interest
options.D: Crossed arms and a tense face

questions.explanation: Crossed arms and a tense face. Crossed arms, a frown, or a tight jaw often signal frustration or defensiveness. Smiling, nodding, and leaning forward usually show comfort, agreement, and interest.

performanceIndicator.text: Interpret others' nonverbal cues

questions.question: A hotel places cards in rooms inviting guests to reuse towels instead of having them washed daily. The main goal of this program is to

options.A: increase room rates.
options.C: limit the number of towels guests can have.
options.D: save time for front desk staff.

questions.explanation: Reduce water and energy use. Washing fewer towels saves water, energy, and detergent, reducing the hotel's environmental impact. The program doesn't affect the front desk, raise rates, or restrict guests, who can still request fresh towels.

performanceIndicator.text: Identify environmental sustainability issues in hospitality and tourism

questions.question: In the hospitality and tourism industry, the product is often

options.A: identical from one customer to the next.
options.B: a durable good that lasts for years.
options.C: an experience rather than a physical good.
options.D: something customers can store at home.

questions.explanation: An experience rather than a physical good. Hospitality products, such as a hotel stay, a meal, or a tour, are largely intangible experiences that are consumed as they are delivered. They can't be stored, they don't last for years, and they vary depending on the employee, the guest, and the situation.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the concept of product in the hospitality and tourism industry

questions.question: A resort receives thousands of social media comments each month. What makes analyzing these comments challenging?

options.A: They are already sorted by topic
options.B: They are never related to the resort
options.C: They are unstructured text and images
options.D: They contain only numbers

questions.explanation: They are unstructured text and images. Free-form text and images don't follow a set format, so analyzing them requires tools that interpret language and sentiment. The comments aren't numbers, aren't pre-sorted, and often discuss the resort directly.

performanceIndicator.text: Identify challenges with the use of unstructured business data

questions.question: Which of the following should an employee do first when a guest complains that the room is noisy:

options.A: Explain that the hotel is always noisy
options.B: Blame the guests in the next room
options.C: Listen and apologize for the inconvenience
options.D: Tell the guest to check out

questions.explanation: Listen and apologize for the inconvenience. Listening and apologizing shows the guest that the complaint is taken seriously, which calms the situation and opens the way to a solution, such as a room change. Making excuses, blaming others, or telling the guest to leave makes the conflict worse.

performanceIndicator.text: Resolve hospitality and tourism related conflicts for customers

questions.question: Why might a hotel request references from other customers before choosing a new laundry vendor?

options.A: To find out the vendor's favorite foods
options.B: To learn whether the vendor is reliable
options.C: To avoid signing a contract
options.D: To lower its own room rates

questions.explanation: To learn whether the vendor is reliable. References show how the vendor has performed for others, including reliability, quality, and problem resolution. They don't reveal personal preferences, set room rates, or remove the need for a contract.

performanceIndicator.text: Select vendors

questions.question: A boutique hotel lists "local, sustainable, and personal" as its core values. Which action best communicates these values to guests?

options.A: Serving breakfast made from local farm food
options.C: Using imported bottled water in every room
options.D: Offering the same generic décor as chain hotels

questions.explanation: Serving breakfast made from local farm food. Locally sourced food demonstrates the hotel's values in a way guests can experience. Imported bottled water conflicts with sustainability and local sourcing, kiosks reduce personal service, and generic décor doesn't reflect the hotel's distinct identity.

performanceIndicator.text: Communicate core values of product/service

questions.question: Which of the following best describes excellent customer service in a hotel:

options.A: Doing only what the job description requires
options.B: Serving guests as quickly as possible no matter what
options.C: Following rules even when they harm guests
options.D: Meeting or exceeding guest expectations

questions.explanation: Meeting or exceeding guest expectations. Excellent service means understanding what guests expect and delivering it or more. Doing the bare minimum, applying rules rigidly, and focusing only on speed can all leave guests unsatisfied.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the nature of customer service in the hospitality and tourism industry

questions.question: Which of the following is a service offered by the lodging sector of the hospitality industry:

options.A: Theme park admission
options.C: Overnight accommodations
options.D: Rental car insurance coverage

questions.explanation: Overnight accommodations. Lodging businesses, such as hotels, resorts, and inns, provide places to stay overnight, often with related services like dining. Airline flights belong to transportation, rental car insurance to travel services, and theme parks to recreation.

performanceIndicator.text: Describe services offered by the hospitality and tourism industry

questions.question: Which of the following should an employee do when serving guests from different cultures:

options.A: Be aware of cultural differences
options.C: Speak louder to be understood
options.D: Use slang and idioms

questions.explanation: Be aware of cultural differences. Cultures differ in greetings, personal space, eye contact, and directness. Being aware of these differences helps employees communicate respectfully. Speaking louder doesn't help understanding, slang can confuse, and ignoring differences may offend guests.

performanceIndicator.text: Adapt communication to the cultural and social differences among clients

questions.question: Which of the following should an employee do when processing a special order, such as a custom birthday cake:

options.A: Collect payment without noting the order details
options.C: Rely on remembering what the customer said
options.D: Make the cake however the bakery prefers

questions.explanation: Confirm the details in writing. Special orders involve specific requests, so written confirmation prevents mistakes and gives both the customer and staff a clear record. Relying on memory, ignoring the customer's wishes, or skipping details often leads to errors.

performanceIndicator.text: Process special orders in hospitality and tourism

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a product extension in the hospitality industry:

options.A: A hotel closes its swimming pool for the winter
options.B: A cruise line raises its prices
options.C: An airline reduces the number of flights it offers
options.D: A restaurant starts selling its sauces in grocery stores

questions.explanation: A restaurant starts selling its sauces in grocery stores. Selling a restaurant's sauces in stores extends its brand to a new product and market. Closing a pool, raising prices, and cutting flights change existing operations but do not extend the product line.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the nature of product extensions in the hospitality and tourism industry

questions.question: Why would a hotel's sales manager use an integrated software package to prepare a proposal?

options.A: It works only on paper
options.B: It prevents her from adding charts or graphs to a report
options.C: She can move spreadsheet tables into documents
options.D: It requires her to retype all data

questions.explanation: She can move spreadsheet tables into documents. Integrated applications share data smoothly, so tables and charts can be moved into documents and slides without retyping. They reduce rather than add work, support charts, and are digital tools.

performanceIndicator.text: Use an integrated business software application package

questions.question: Which of the following is a right that workers in the United States have:

options.A: A workplace free of serious hazards
options.C: A guaranteed promotion every year
options.D: The right to set their own wages

questions.explanation: A workplace free of serious hazards. Federal law gives workers the right to a safe workplace, along with rights such as minimum wage and freedom from discrimination. Annual promotions, setting one's own pay, and unlimited vacation are not legal rights.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the rights of workers

questions.question: A guest asks a resort's restaurant to prepare a dish that isn't on the menu for a family member's dietary needs. The server should

options.A: say no without asking anyone.
options.C: promise the dish will be ready without checking.
options.D: check with the kitchen first.

questions.explanation: Check with the kitchen first. The kitchen knows whether it has the ingredients and time to prepare the request. Checking first allows the server to give an honest answer. Refusing outright, promising without checking, or overcharging all lead to poor guest experiences.

performanceIndicator.text: Process special orders in hospitality and tourism

questions.question: Which opening sentence would be most effective in a letter of application for a hotel front desk position?

options.A: "I'm excited to apply for Harbor View's front desk role."
options.B: "I saw something online about a job opening at your hotel."
options.C: "You should hire me because I'm the best person you'll ever meet."
options.D: "Hey, I need a job."

questions.explanation: "I'm excited to apply for Harbor View's front desk role." An effective opening names the specific position and the employer and sets a professional, enthusiastic tone. The other sentences are too casual, boastful, or vague.

performanceIndicator.text: Write a letter of application

questions.question: An integrated software package typically combines

options.A: several applications in one suite.
options.C: hardware and furniture.
options.D: a single calculator program.

questions.explanation: Several applications in one suite. Integrated packages bundle several applications that share a common interface and can easily exchange data, such as inserting a spreadsheet chart into a report. Antivirus software, hardware, and a single calculator aren't integrated suites.

performanceIndicator.text: Use an integrated business software application package

questions.question: In a database, a single piece of information such as a guest's last name is stored in a

options.A: report.
options.C: query.
options.D: form.

questions.explanation: Field. A field holds one type of data, such as a last name, within a record. A report presents data in a printable format, a query asks the database a question, and a form is an on-screen layout for entering data.

performanceIndicator.text: Demonstrate basic database applications

questions.question: A hotel ran a project to reduce check-in time to under five minutes. Which data would best show whether the project succeeded?

options.A: The cost of the lobby furniture
options.B: The number of rooms in the hotel
options.C: Check-in times before and after
options.D: Guests' favorite room colors

questions.explanation: Check-in times before and after. Comparing check-in times before and after the change directly measures whether the goal was met. Room counts, color preferences, and furniture costs aren't related to the project's goal.

performanceIndicator.text: Evaluate project results

questions.question: Which of the following is a factor associated with positive customer experiences:

options.A: Long wait times without explanation
options.B: Employees who are friendly and helpful
options.C: Rules that are not explained to customers
options.D: Inconsistent service from visit to visit

questions.explanation: Employees who are friendly and helpful. Friendly, helpful employees make guests feel welcome and valued, a major driver of positive experiences. Unexplained waits, inconsistency, and confusing rules frustrate customers.

performanceIndicator.text: Identify factors associated with positive customer experiences

questions.question: Which of the following is a source of secondary hospitality and tourism information:

options.A: A survey a hotel conducts with its own guests
options.C: A focus group held by a restaurant
options.D: Observations of guests in a hotel lobby

questions.explanation: A government tourism spending report. Secondary information has already been collected by someone else for another purpose, such as government tourism reports. Surveys, observations, and focus groups conducted by the business itself produce primary information.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain sources of secondary hospitality and tourism information

questions.question: The construction of the interstate highway system in the United States led to growth in

options.A: long-distance passenger train travel.
options.C: roadside motels and restaurants.
options.D: ocean cruise lines and ports.

questions.explanation: Roadside motels and restaurants. Highways made road trips easier, creating demand for motels, gas stations, and restaurants along the routes. Cruises, train travel, and space tourism weren't driven by the highway system, and passenger rail actually declined as car travel grew.

performanceIndicator.text: Describe the development of the hospitality and tourism industry

questions.question: A ski resort offers a lower lift-ticket price on weekdays than on weekends. What is the main reason for this pricing strategy?

options.A: To cover the cost of new lifts in one season
options.B: To make weekends less crowded by raising costs
options.C: To match the prices charged by grocery stores
options.D: To attract more guests during slower times

questions.explanation: To attract more guests during slower times. Lower weekday prices encourage guests to visit when demand is lower, which spreads out business and fills capacity that would otherwise go unused. The strategy focuses on weekdays, isn't tied to a single equipment purchase, and has nothing to do with grocery prices.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the concept of price in the hospitality and tourism industry

questions.question: Guests who arrive at the Meridian Hotel before check-in time leave their cell number at the desk. The hotel's software then texts each guest as soon as housekeeping marks the room clean. The hotel is using technology to

options.A: hire front desk employees.
options.C: train housekeeping staff.
options.D: set room prices.

questions.explanation: Automate a guest service. Automating routine messages saves staff time and keeps guests informed without a phone call. Pricing, training, and hiring are separate functions that this messaging software doesn't perform.

performanceIndicator.text: Use software to automate services

questions.question: Which of the following is an advantage for a business that accepts credit cards:

options.A: Customers may spend more than they would with cash
options.C: There are no fees for processing credit cards
options.D: Credit card sales are not taxed

questions.explanation: Customers may spend more than they would with cash. Accepting cards is convenient for customers and often leads to larger purchases. However, businesses pay processing fees, customers can dispute charges, and card sales are taxed like any other sale.

performanceIndicator.text: Discuss considerations in accepting credit-card payments

questions.question: A guest wants to pay for a large purchase using several different credit cards, each declined until the last one works. What should the employee do?

options.A: Ignore it because the last card worked
options.B: Follow company policy for possible fraud and alert a manager
options.C: Ask the guest for the cards' PINs
options.D: Process every card until one works without saying anything

questions.explanation: Follow company policy for possible fraud and alert a manager. Multiple declined cards can be a sign of stolen card numbers. Following procedures and involving a manager protects the business. Asking for PINs violates security rules, and ignoring warning signs could leave the business with fraud losses.

performanceIndicator.text: Identify credit card fraud prevention methods

questions.question: A new hotel sales coordinator notices that the head chef strongly influences which events the hotel accepts, even though the chef isn't her supervisor. To work effectively, she should

options.A: make decisions without consulting anyone.
options.B: ignore the chef because he isn't her boss.
options.C: build a good relationship with the chef.
options.D: complain to guests about the chef.

questions.explanation: Build a good relationship with the chef. Understanding who has informal influence helps employees work more effectively. Building a positive relationship with the chef can help her events succeed. Ignoring him, complaining to guests, or acting alone could create conflict.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the impact of political relationships within an organization

questions.question: In the kitchen at Oliveto Trattoria, cooks put food scraps in a compost bin, flatten cardboard boxes for recycling, and place glass bottles in a separate container before taking out the trash. The kitchen staff is

options.A: cross-contaminating food.
options.C: reducing menu prices.
options.D: inventory forecasting.

questions.explanation: Sorting waste properly. Sorting waste at its source makes recycling and composting possible and keeps kitchens clean and sanitary. Cross-contamination is the spread of harmful bacteria to food, and waste sorting doesn't affect menu prices or inventory forecasts.

performanceIndicator.text: Practice safe and sanitary handling/disposal of wastes/recyclables

questions.question: A popular brunch restaurant has hour-long waits on Sunday mornings. Which strategy would best improve guests' experience during this peak?

options.A: Text guests when their table is ready
options.C: Refuse to seat anyone who arrives after 9 a.m.
options.D: Make guests wait outside with no updates

questions.explanation: Text guests when their table is ready. Texting lets guests wait comfortably and reduces the sense of a long wait, which improves satisfaction during busy times. Turning guests away, giving no updates, and ignoring calls would frustrate customers and lose business.

performanceIndicator.text: Identify strategies to manage customer experience during peaks in demand

questions.question: For a restaurant, which of the following is part of its supply chain?

options.A: The farm growing its vegetables
options.C: Its online customer reviews
options.D: Its employee break room schedule

questions.explanation: The farm growing its vegetables. A restaurant's supply chain includes farms, food distributors, and delivery companies that provide its ingredients. Reviews, break rooms, and menu design aren't part of how ingredients reach the kitchen.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the concept of supply chain

questions.question: In the hospitality industry, promotion is used to

options.A: clean and maintain facilities.
options.B: set the price of hotel rooms.
options.C: hire seasonal employees.
options.D: inform and persuade customers.

questions.explanation: Inform and persuade customers. Promotion communicates with customers through advertising, social media, publicity, and sales promotions to build awareness and encourage bookings. Pricing, maintenance, and hiring are other business activities.

performanceIndicator.text: Describe the concept of promotion in the hospitality and tourism industry
